notes: Overturn confirmed, as PARTIAL (the format and SR1's value range are implemented; the form of the operand is not). The format's operand is a segment-number, and the standard defines that user-defined word: 'A segment-number may be expressed either as a one or two digit number' (III.2). SR1 bounds its value. No other text states a form, and none conflicts with the definition. III.1 says the glossary definitions are brief and leave detailed syntactical rules to Sections IV to XVI, but that does not make them non-normative. Here the definition is the only statement of what a segment-number looks like, so a three-digit word is not one. The same compiler enforces the identical one-or-two-digit form for level-numbers (COBOL1746 on '001'). Rerun: SEGMENT-LIMIT IS 010 and IS 001, and SECTION 020, compile and run. IS 09 compiles, which is right. Own probe: SECTION 007 compiles (it should be refused) and SECTION 07 compiles (right). ScreenSegmentNumber checks only the integer's value. Harm is under-rejection only; no program changes meaning. The note PB5379 is right in its citations, its expected result and its site. The section-header sibling it names (XVI.3.2.2 and XVI.3.2.3) belongs to the same fix. kb/Work PB5379 holds the defect (adjudication: held-85/set5/decisions.json).

next.reason: 1985: "SEGMENT-LIMIT IS segment-number"; 2023: "No 2023 clause carries the Segmentation module or the SEGMENT-LIMIT clause; no candidate covers it.". No 2023 clause holds the Segmentation feature, and no candidate by wording covers SEGMENT-LIMIT, so the 2023 standard lacks the clause.
